# Results and Discussion

## Calculations

[Description of analysis performed]

**Equation used:**

$$
y = mx + b
$$ {#eq-linear}

**Sample calculation:**

For the first data point where $x = 0.0044151$ m and $V = 0.0030871$ V:

$$
\begin{aligned}
y &= mx + b \\
  &= (0.5)(0.0044151) + 0.001 \\
  &= 0.0032076 \text{ V}
\end{aligned}
$$

```{python}
#| label: fig-results
#| fig-cap: "Voltage vs. Position showing linear relationship"
#| fig-width: 6
#| fig-height: 4.5

# Prepare data for plotting
x = np.array([0.0044151, 0.0021633, 0.0003600, 0.0023831])
V = np.array([0.0030871, 0.0021343, 0.0018642, 0.0013287])

# Perform linear fit
coeffs = np.polyfit(x, V, 1)
fit_line = np.poly1d(coeffs)
x_fit = np.linspace(x.min(), x.max(), 100)

# Create figure
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(6, 4.5))

# Plot data and fit
ax.plot(x, V, 'o', markersize=8, label='Experimental data', 
        markerfacecolor='none', markeredgewidth=1.5, markeredgecolor='C0')
ax.plot(x_fit, fit_line(x_fit), '-', linewidth=1.5, 
        label=f'Linear fit: $V = {coeffs[0]:.4f}x + {coeffs[1]:.6f}$')

# Labels and formatting
ax.set_xlabel(r'Position, $x$ (m)', fontsize=11)
ax.set_ylabel(r'Voltage, $V$ (V)', fontsize=11)
ax.legend(loc='best', frameon=True, fontsize=10)
ax.grid(True, alpha=0.3, linestyle='--')
ax.tick_params(labelsize=10)

plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()
```
